stirling-relevant-input-dedup-review.text:
# Relevant-input deduplication review

Verdict: the intended durable-input rule is reasonable, but the current core does not enforce it for unchanged arrivals. It deduplicates changed outputs at their successor. An unchanged path can reach a relevant instruction without admitting its input to that instruction's store. The instruction can then execute twice on an identical input, with only its outputs deduplicated.

Clean runtime: `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005`. The clean Stirling campaign reached run-6, completed run-5 and accepted the run-5 report. This review reads source and the already-run isolated diagnostic test; it makes no runtime change or new analyzer run.

## Where the durable gate is applied

```kotlin
// RunMethodAnalyzer.emitCovered: output of the instruction being processed.
forEachSuccessor(node) { successor ->
    edges.add(successor, premise, facts)?.let {
        push(EdgeDelta(premise, successor, it))
    }
}

// RunMethodAnalyzer.emitUnchanged: no durable admission at successor.
forEachSuccessor(item.node) { successor ->
    if (worklist.addUnchanged(EdgeDelta(item.premise, successor, item.facts)))
        requestWork()
}

// RunMethodAnalyzer.process: no input-store test before interpreting this item.
steps++
if (context.callAt(item.node) != null) callServices.process(item)
else runStatement(item)
```

`MethodEdgeStore` keys its complete values by statement and full premise. It does not classify a target as relevant and intercept all arrivals. The producer's `emitCovered` versus `emitUnchanged` path determines whether the target input was durably admitted.

`DeltaWorklist.seen` is not that durable input store. It is cleared when the unchanged lanes empty, even while changed work remains. Thus “all unchanged facts have reached a relevant point” applies to the current wave, not to every pending producer.

## Verified minimal production-core case

The existing isolated `RelevantInputDedupInvestigationTest` uses the actual `RunMethodAnalyzer`, `MethodEdgeStore`, worklist and statement forms. It first obtains its one run-5 concrete initial from the actual DemandStore emitter:

```text
incoming demand: p.$/T -> ret.$/T
submitted fact: p.$/T, NORMAL
admitted initial I: p.$/T
```

Its AP CFG is:

```text
               1: y = p -> 3: neutral --\
0: branch                               5: return y -> 6: normal exit
               2: y = p -> 4: neutral --/
```

Both copy instructions have the exact same canonical p and y bases. This is an explicit tested AP CFG, not an assumption that every Java frontend preserves a source-level y across branch SSA conversion.

For the y relation, the valid queue construction is:

```text
Input at0: I -> p.$/T, NORMAL.
0 passes p unchanged to1 and2.

2 executes y=p:
  admits I -> y.$/T at successor4; queues changed4/y.
1 executes y=p:
  admits I -> y.$/T at successor3; queues changed3/y.

These are different durable destination keys: (4,I) and (3,I).
Neither admission is a duplicate at that point.

3/y passes unchanged to5/y, without edges.add(5,I,y/T).
5 executes return y; its ret/T output is admitted at6.
The unchanged lane empties; seen clears while4/y remains pending.

4/y passes unchanged to5/y, again without edges.add(5,I,y/T).
5 executes the identical return input again.
Its ret/T output at6 is now a duplicate and is discarded.
```

The executed test confirms:

| CFG | Identical relevant y-input visits at5 | Stored y-input rows at5 | Ret-output visits at6 | Stored ret rows at6 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Copies go directly to5 |1|1|1|1|
| Neutral nodes3/4 between copy and5 |2|0|1|1|

The test checks equality of the two complete relevant inputs in the padded case. It also checks that another work call after draining does not increase steps. One test, zero failures/errors/skips, timestamp2026-10-30T00:12:26, duration0.091s.

The unpadded control is important. If two changed outputs both enter5 directly, `edges.add(5,...)` correctly admits only one. My earlier finite source-branch illustration was incomplete unless it stated distinct admitted successors before the common unchanged route. It must not be read as assuming duplicate changed packets can bypass a shared successor's existing gate.

A source-shaped variant can keep the same p base without assigning it across branches:

```java
Box p = sourceT();
if (choose) inspect(p.f);  // Field read retains p; inspect takes the field value.
else        inspect(p.g); // Same p; a different read result local.
sinkT(p);
```

`MicroEdgeBuilder.read` keeps its source p through `keep(p)`. The copy/read output is admitted at each branch's next instruction. For the p fact, the following inspect call is untouched because its operand is the field-result local, not p. Its p input can therefore enter the common sink through the unchanged path. This variant is a reasoned source analogue; the executed regression uses the explicit core CFG above.

## What this proves, and what it does not

It proves a relevant instruction can process an identical full input twice. Input deduplication is not universal in the current core. It also proves the output gate can preserve the resulting fixed point in this case: one return result remains. This is avoidable repeated evaluation, not evidence of a missing result or an infinite loop.

It does not prove that every repeated neutral visit is duplicate useful work. Two routes can legitimately need to carry a fresh relation to its first relevant operation. Counting repeated pass-through visits alone does not identify how many rule, call or transfer evaluations are repeated.

The actual PipelineProcessor witness at464 is a body fact at `parameters.entrySet()`. That operation does not touch the body base, so the witness proves repeated neutral routing. It does not by itself prove duplicate evaluation at the next body-relevant operation. The new production-core test closes the generic possibility, but the diagnostic did not record the exact preceding producer and next relevant endpoint for each Pipeline witness.

Likewise, clearing the repeat set is a verified enabling condition, not a proved standalone attribution for the entire1.575-billion unchanged workload. Some routing is necessary; some is repeated; the exact proportions at relevant endpoints are not measured.

## Implication for a fix

The intended invariant is:

```text
Every relevant input membership is admitted once at that operation,
including arrivals that crossed untouched instructions.
```

A future implementation can gate unchanged arrivals when they reach a relevant endpoint, or maintain a distinct processed-input membership store. It must not blindly call the existing input store on every pop: changed items were already admitted, and that would discard their first processing too. It must retain pointwise protection updates, full premises and the existing standing rule/callee replay mechanisms.

This review selects no implementation. It establishes the missing current gate and the limits of the existing measured attribution.

stirling-user-dedup-invariant-audit.text:
# Audit: relevant-input deduplication and the Stirling repeat claim

Date: 2026-10-30. Read-only source audit of runtime `bb74cef6cf483db167c161020a8a4cca576ca005` and the closed diagnostic evidence. Latest Stirling reached run-6, complete run-5; run-6 TIMEOUT. No runtime edit or analyzer launch.

## Main correction

The current evidence proves repeated complete keys and a mechanism which permits repeated neutral prefixes. It does not prove that those duplicates account for most of the 1.575 billion unchanged visits, and it does not identify the producer of the 6.33 million changed items. A small demand frontier, 147 initials, and seven-node packets do not bound the number of distinct field words or statement memberships.

The user's input-deduplication intuition is partly correct: equal changed outputs at one successor are durably deduplicated. But the code does **not** have a uniform durable input gate immediately before each relevant instruction. An unchanged arrival bypasses MethodEdgeStore, even if its target instruction will be relevant. Repeated inputs can therefore execute the relevant transfer again; the resulting outputs may then be rejected as duplicates.

## Exact source path

```text
runStatement/processCall
  if the current base is untouched:
      emitUnchanged -> worklist.addUnchanged(successor/input)
      // no MethodEdgeStore admission at the successor
  else:
      evaluate transfers / filters / rules / call stages
      emitAfter -> edges.add(successor, premise, result)
      push only the fresh point-store delta
```

Source locations:

* `RunMethodAnalyzer.runStatement:551–558`, `emitCovered:568–573`, `emitUnchanged:576–583`.
* `RunMethodCallServices.process:55–67` has the same base/touched split; it does not check MethodEdgeStore before executing a relevant call plan. Subscription input deduplication is inside a later call stage, not a universal instruction-input gate.
* `FormApplier.statement:47–61` sends an untouched base to the unchanged callback. A touched base executes its forms before the resulting successor store admission.
* `MethodEdgeStore.add:36–65` is a real durable deduplication/coverage gate, but only its callers use it. It returns new geometry, new annotation support, or null; unchanged admissions do not call it.
* `DeltaWorklist.addUnchanged:50–61` performs short-lived exact-key suppression, with a separate protection mask; `afterProcess:123–126` clears that set when unchanged lanes empty, regardless of changed work.

An input which was already admitted as changed must not be blindly re-added at `process` time: its presence in the store includes queued, not necessarily processed, work. Such a naive gate could suppress the first actual processing. A proposed uniform gate needs one admission boundary or separate discovered/processed semantics.

## A relevant copy cuts the repeated traversal

`MicroEdgeBuilder.move:49–56` implements `z = x` with both `keep(x)` and `x -> z`. Both results use `emitAfter`, so both reach the durable successor gate.

```java
while (condition) {
    // F = I -> x.sigma/T may walk N instructions unchanged.
    z = x;  // relevant to F
            // attempt I -> x.sigma/T and I -> z.sigma/T at the successor
            // both results go through MethodEdgeStore.add
}
```

If the full original premise, fact header, geometry, marks and mask are unchanged, a second execution of this copy cannot repeatedly enqueue the same two outputs at the same successor. The duplicate traversal stops there. A single closed unchanged loop is also suppressed within its wave. Thus reset alone is not a proof of an endless loop or unlimited work from one fixed producer.

This matters for the actual witness: PipelineProcessor nodes 464–482 leave body var(92) untouched; node 483 copies it. An equal arrival can waste that neutral prefix and re-evaluate the copy, but its ordinary copy outputs are still deduplicated. The exact preceding changed producer of the sampled node-464 repeat was not logged. That missing edge in the causal trace remains important.

## A valid multi-wave pattern despite output deduplication

The queue-only finite example is realizable only if the producers' stored outputs are at **different** points before the common untouched region:

```text
                  copy C1 -- private neutral P1 --\
                 /                               \
input F --------+-- copy C2 -- private neutral P2 ---- J -> N shared neutral nodes -> R
                 \                               /
                  copy CK -- private neutral PK -/
```

Each Ci is relevant and preserves F beside its copied target. Its successor Pi is distinct, so `edges.add(Pi,F)` can succeed once for every i. Pi routes F unchanged to J. J and the common region have no durable input admission. Once one unchanged wave drains and the repeat set clears, another pending Pi can route the same complete F through J and the same N nodes. R is the next relevant operation, whose identical outputs can all be rejected after the first one.

The potential work is K×N for F even with only one initial and one field word. If every Ci instead submitted F **directly to the same J through emitAfter**, `edges.add(J,F)` would admit it once and the model would not reproduce K waves. The private untouched ingress is essential. This is a mechanism example, not a source-bound assertion about the hot PipelineProcessor producer.

## “Changed” is not identical to “new globally visited relation”

A second asymmetry affects interpretation of the 6.33 million changed items:

```text
first arm:   untouched path -> J/F processes without storing J/F
second arm:  relevant copy -> preserved F -> edges.add(J,F)
```

The second arm can obtain a fresh durable admission although J/F was already processed through the first arm. The point store's meaning is “first stored coverage here,” not “never processed here before.” Thus the changed counter can contain:

1. genuinely new marked field words;
2. the first occurrence at a new instruction;
3. a first durable insertion of a relation previously visited unchanged;
4. a required field/mark-exclusion or protection upgrade.

The hot run-5 owner has no protection masks, but the other distinctions remain. Taint/Flow groups also return residual packets, not a universal census of distinct original complete packets. Neither all changed work nor all unchanged work can be labelled redundant from these counters alone.

## Production-actor control

The parent ran `RelevantInputDedupInvestigationTest` in the isolated diagnostic checkout; it passed. It uses the real run-5 actor with a valid C2 `p.$/T` initial from the exact paired demand `p.$/T -> ret.$/T`, not a queue-only mock.

```text
Diamond copies y=p -> private untouched pads 3/4 -> relevant return at 5:
    identical node-5 y inputs processed = 2
    node-5 y durable store entries      = 0
    returned ret at node 6 processed   = 1; durable store entries = 1

Same diamond, direct copies to return 5, without pads:
    node-5 y inputs processed = 1; durable store entries = 1
    returned ret at node 6 processed = 1
```

This confirms the source distinction: relevant inputs can be recomputed after untouched arrivals while their equal outputs are filtered. It does not measure the fraction of Stirling work attributable to this mechanism. No full-project rerun is part of this control. This child did not launch the test.

## Adversarial interpretation of the measurements

The hot owner has 1,575,082,922 unchanged visits and 7,751,326 sampled exact repeated processed keys across reset epochs. The witnessed lower bound is about **0.492%** of its unchanged visits. The hash-selected bounded LRU is biased and lossy. Multiplying this percentage by 64 or extrapolating it to all nodes is invalid.

It is therefore consistent with the current measurements that cross-wave exact duplicate removal saves only a modest fraction and most work still serves fresh combinations. It is also consistent that unrecorded duplicates are much more numerous. The data do not decide between those cases. The 248.7 unchanged/changed ratio shows routing amplification, not an exact duplicate percentage or a measured neutral-region length.

There are two separate work-removal questions:

* **Duplicate suppression:** which already processed relations re-enter a common region, from which distinct durable ingress points? This needs equality coverage and join/protection/notification preservation.
* **Neutral-region compression:** how many neutral nodes does each required fresh relation visit before its next relevant boundary? This can remove work even if every region input is new. It still needs a certified neutral region, including rule observations and closed cycles; “unchanged” does not by itself mean no rule can observe the fact.

The latter opportunity does not depend on proving a high duplicate percentage. Neither opportunity eliminates genuinely new model/alias field combinations. The run-6 mixed-field-word investigation is a separate potential generator reduction; its precise producer and safe typed pruning contract remain unresolved.

## Minimal missing evidence

Do not run another broad profile merely to reconfirm `emitUnchanged` is hot. The discriminating trace would record, for a bounded exact-key sample at the relevant boundary and common region entry:

```text
(full premise, full fact/header, protection mask, node)
previously processed?  previously durably stored?
arrival kind: changed / unchanged
producer node and producer operation kind
changed-store result: null / new geometry / annotation upgrade
new path word or a repeat of earlier unchanged coverage?
```

Use the actual node 483 copy and its output successor as a first boundary, plus node 464 and the producer which re-enters it. Count first-time versus repeated unchanged visits per neutral region, and changed outputs rejected versus accepted. This separates duplicate prefixes from fresh-word routing without claiming every equal-looking relation can be discarded. Any future gate must preserve late joins, standing subscriptions, observers, exclusions, layers and protection upgrades.

Recommended report wording: “The current queue/store split permits repeated neutral prefixes and the probe confirms some exact repeats. It has not yet established the removable fraction or the fresh producer behind the hot owner's relation growth.”

limits: A finite production-actor fixture, not a real-project performance experiment.
The Java outline denotes the tested CFG and data forms; no exact javac lowering claim.
Output deduplication and closure remain intact; relevant input evaluation can repeat after unchanged arrivals.
The earlier sampled duplicate count does not establish the global redundant-work fraction.
